Answer Choices: (A) Ankle plantar flexion (B) Hip flexion (C) Ankle eversion (D) Great toe dorsiflexion (E) Hip external rotation (F) Knee flexion (G) Ankle plantarflexion (H) Knee extension (I) Foot pronation (J) Ankle inversion

Prioritize surgical anatomy and clinical case evidence.'}

The **L5 nerve root** is most at risk. It courses across the anterior surface of the sacral ala, so an iliosacral screw that penetrates anteriorly can compress or injure it; the S1 root is more closely related to the S1 foramen. Clinical reports describe anteriorly malpositioned screws causing **unilateral L5-root compression and foot drop**.[^1]

Among the listed motor functions, the best answer is:

**Great toe dorsiflexion (extension)** — principally testing the L5 myotome through the extensor hallucis longus.

Ankle eversion can also be weakened with L5 injury, but **great-toe dorsiflexion is the most characteristic and specific choice**.
